items.question: A new C# service on the host needs to read game-server status and issue start/stop commands. Per the ecosystem's dependency rules, how should it talk to the kgsm engine?
choices: Shell out to kgsm.sh directly with Process.Start
Go through kgsm-lib, the single C#-to-engine chokepoint
Open the kgsm event unix socket and parse the stream itself
Call the Control Panel web API and let it relay the command
items.gold: kgsm-lib (C#, Native-AOT): The single C#-to-KGSM chokepoint — process-exec + JSON + event socket to typed C#, no matter what. Consumed by every C# component: monitor, assistant, web API, and the Discord bot.

items.question: The ecosystem holds a hard rule that one component violated, which is the reason the original kgsm-api was scrapped. What was the violation?
choices: It depended on a sibling leaf service instead of the aggregator
It used Native AOT where standard JIT was mandated
It invented metrics and status instead of measuring them
It bound an authenticated network socket the design forbade
items.gold: Server is authoritative; never fabricate. No component invents a metric, status, or alert — measured or unknown. This killed kgsm-api; it's why the monitor reads /proc not top.

items.question: The aggregator shows a server for which the monitor currently has no metrics row. What is it allowed to conclude about that server's run-state?
choices: That the server is stopped
That the server has crashed
Nothing about run-state — absence means 'not measurable right now', not 'stopped'
That the server is running but idle
items.gold: Metric-presence is never a status. A surface joins status-from-the-authority with metrics-from-the-monitor, and never infers run-state from whether a metrics row exists — absence means 'not measurable right now,' not 'stopped.'

items.question: kgsm-watchdog is described as deliberately breaking one of the system-wide invariants, accepted eyes-open. Which invariant does it break?
choices: Never fabricate a metric or status
The kgsm CLI stays stateless
Leaves are independently deployable
Sampling stays O(1) in client count
items.gold: The kgsm CLI stays stateless; the watchdog is the contained exception. The kgsm-watchdog is the one resident, stateful piece (desired-state + warm process) — accepted eyes-open as the engine's runtime half, not a leaf.

items.question: How does kgsm-monitor control access to the socket it serves metrics on?
choices: Discord-OAuth, like the network-facing services
A bearer token kept in the client's sessionStorage
It authenticates nothing; access is gated by filesystem permissions only
Mutual TLS between monitor and aggregator
items.gold: The monitor runs root, exposes an unauthenticated socket gated by FS perms only — it authenticates nothing. The network-facing services (web API, assistant) enforce Discord-OAuth.

items.question: When many clients want live metrics, where does the design put the fan-out, and what does the monitor itself do?
choices: In the monitor, which pushes a stream to each connected client
In the web API; the monitor samples once and serves the latest snapshot
In the SPA, which polls the monitor socket directly
In kgsm-lib, which caches per consumer
items.gold: Sampling stays O(1) in client count. Fan-out lives in the web API; the monitor samples once and serves latest.

items.question: Most of the .NET ecosystem targets Native AOT. Which component is the deliberate, eyes-open exception, and what stack does it use?
choices: kgsm-monitor, which falls back to JIT for /proc parsing
The kgsm-api web aggregator, which uses standard JIT with controllers + EF Core
kgsm-lib, which ships a JIT build specifically for the bot
The assistant CLI, which is JIT-only for plugin support
items.gold: Built in kgsm-api on standard JIT — controllers + EF Core, the deliberate exception to the AOT ecosystem (not embedded; eyes-open maintainability trade).

items.question: kgsm-lib reaches the kgsm-firewall authority over a unix socket. What wire format does that seam use, and why not HTTP?
choices: HTTP/1.1 over the unix socket, reusing the watchdog's ASP.NET stack
gRPC, for typed contracts
NDJSON over UDS, because the firewall authority carries no ASP.NET stack
Raw protobuf over a TCP loopback port
items.gold: kgsm-lib to kgsm-firewall: NDJSON over UDS (not HTTP — the authority carries no ASP.NET stack); wire shared as the TheKrystalShip.KGSM.Firewall.Contracts package.

items.question: A native instance is started on the host today. Which component carries out the start, and which one emits the lifecycle event observers see?
choices: kgsm performs the start and kgsm emits the event
kgsm-watchdog performs the start, and kgsm still emits the event
kgsm-lib performs the start and the watchdog emits the event
The monitor performs the start and kgsm-lib emits the event
items.gold: Native lifecycle (start/stop/is-active/enable) now routes through kgsm-watchdog; kgsm still owns event emission. Watchdog acts, kgsm emits, monitor/bot observe.

items.question: What is the kgsm-web repository today?
choices: A deprecated React/Node admin panel kept only as a dead end
The Control Panel SPA, a standard Vite + React 18 build
The per-host aggregator web API
The Discord bot surface onto the assistant
items.gold: React SPA (Control Panel): Lives in kgsm-web — a standard Vite + React 18 (JSX) build ported from the krystal-design prototype. The stale React/Node admin panel that previously lived here was discarded and replaced in-place.

items.question: Following XDG conventions, where do a user's deployed kgsm game-server instances live on disk?
choices: /opt/kgsm/instances/
~/.config/kgsm/instances/
~/.local/share/kgsm/instances/
/var/lib/kgsm/servers/
items.gold: KGSM follows XDG Base Directory conventions: ~/.local/share/kgsm/instances/ is where your deployed game servers live; ~/.config/kgsm/config.ini holds global settings.

items.question: KGSM lists an optional package needed for one feature. Which package enables event handling / broadcasting?
choices: ufw, via enable_firewall_management
socat, via enable_event_broadcasting
inotify-tools, which is required not optional
steamcmd, for SteamCMD-based games
items.gold: Optional dependencies: ufw for firewall management (enable_firewall_management=true); socat for event handling (enable_event_broadcasting=true).

items.question: Which command installs the Minecraft blueprint under a custom instance name 'survival'?
choices: kgsm create minecraft survival
kgsm install minecraft --name survival
kgsm blueprints install minecraft survival
kgsm new minecraft=survival
items.gold: Install Minecraft with a custom name: kgsm install minecraft --name survival. Then start it: kgsm start survival.

items.question: How does a .NET project consume kgsm-lib, according to its README?
choices: As a git submodule built from source
As the NuGet package TheKrystalShip.KGSM.Lib
By calling a hosted REST API
By copying the .cs files into the project
items.gold: You can install KGSM-Lib via NuGet: dotnet add package TheKrystalShip.KGSM.Lib.

items.question: Through what mechanism does kgsm-lib deliver real-time KGSM events (installs, startups, shutdowns) to C#?
choices: A polling HTTP endpoint
A Unix Domain Socket
SignalR over WebSockets
A Kafka topic
items.gold: This library simplifies integration with KGSM, as well as listening to real-time events through a Unix Domain Socket.

items.question: During the kgsm-lib migration, IBlueprintService.Create() was removed outright rather than kept or stubbed. Why?
choices: It was renamed to ListDetailed()
kgsm exposes no command to create blueprints, so the lib carried dead code
It was folded into InstanceService.Install()
It broke Native AOT trimming analysis
items.gold: IBlueprintService.Create() removed outright — the lib carries no blueprint-create code at all and kgsm exposes no command to create blueprints, so the bot's dead CreateAsync was deleted.

items.question: What is the central thesis of the architecture review about the kgsm-lib chokepoint?
choices: The chokepoint is the wrong abstraction and should be replaced by a message bus
The chokepoint pattern is correct, but it is operated by hand — the gap is CI/publish/contract-tests, not transport
The chokepoint should be split into one library per consumer
The chokepoint should be removed so consumers talk to kgsm directly
items.gold: The chokepoint is right; it's operated by hand. The gaps are not architectural — they're the missing operational shell around the chokepoint (no CI, no publish step, no contract test). None of this argues for an added message bus.

items.question: The review found the kgsm-lib 1.1.0 release was mislabeled. What was the lesson?
choices: It was fully backward compatible, so the warning was a false alarm
A minor 1.1.0 bump silently shipped source-breaking changes; it warranted a major bump
It dropped Native AOT support without notice
It accidentally re-published 1.0.0-beta under a new number
items.gold: 1.1.0 is NOT backward-compatible with the published 1.0.0-beta, despite its release notes saying 'Backward compatible with 1.0.0.' A minor-version bump silently shipped source-breaking changes; the breaking changes warranted a major bump.

items.question: Which logging framework do all the .NET projects standardize on?
choices: Serilog with structured sinks
NLog
Microsoft.Extensions.Logging (ILogger<T>) only — no Serilog/NLog/log4net
log4net
items.gold: Framework: Microsoft.Extensions.Logging (ILogger<T>) only. No Serilog/NLog/log4net.

items.question: The SystemdConsole formatter prefixes each line with a syslog priority. Which prefix marks an error-level line?
items.gold: It emits <N> syslog priority prefixes (<3> err, <4> warn, <6> info, <7> debug) so journalctl -p err can filter by level.

items.question: How do you turn the log level up to Debug at runtime without editing appsettings.json?
choices: Pass a --log-level Debug flag
Set the environment variable Logging__LogLevel__Default=Debug
Recompile with a DEBUG constant
Edit the journald configuration
items.gold: Default level Information, overridable by environment variables: Logging__LogLevel__Default=Debug (double-underscore is the .NET config convention) wins over the file.

items.question: Why do the kgsm-llm CLI and Eval tools deliberately NOT use the SystemdConsole formatter that the services use?
choices: They are AOT binaries that cannot load the formatter
They are interactive terminal tools; the <N> prefixes look wrong, so they use SimpleConsole routed to stderr
They write logs to a rotating file instead
They disable logging entirely
items.gold: kgsm-llm's CLI and Eval entrypoints are interactive tools, not services. The Systemd formatter's <N> prefixes are meant for journald and look wrong in a terminal. They keep AddSimpleConsole routed to stderr so stdout stays clean.

items.question: Where do the .NET services' logs go, and how is retention handled?
choices: Rotating files under /var/log/kgsm, rotated by the app
To journald, which owns retention; there is no file logging
To a central remote syslog collector by default
To stdout, captured to disk by each service
items.gold: Every project is deployed as a systemd service to journald. No file logging — journald owns retention.

items.question: The gemma4:12b assistant evaluation named the single highest-impact problem. What was it?
choices: The model fabricated server status from the instance list
A kgsm run-state bug — a running server reported as stopped — that the assistant faithfully relays
The model refused to call any tools
Inference latency on the RTX 3060
items.gold: The biggest trust problem in the whole run is not the model — it's a kgsm run-state bug the assistant faithfully relays (a running server reported as stopped). It makes correct model behavior produce wrong answers.

items.question: Concretely, how does that kgsm run-state bug manifest for one running instance?
choices: is-active returns false even though the process is listening
The status command returns false while is-active returns true for the same instance
Both status and is-active return false
The PID file is present but empty
items.gold: The disagreement originates in kgsm itself: its status command returns status: false while is-active returns true for the same instance. The assistant relays the status field, so it inherits the wrong run-state.

items.question: What did the evaluation conclude about editing gemma's system-prompt persona prose?
choices: It never changes gemma-12B's behavior
It moves gemma for concrete, task-relevant routing guidance, though gemma ignored arbitrary style directives
Only changing the temperature changes behavior
It only helps on models above 30B parameters
items.gold: Persona-prose edits do move gemma-12B when the instruction is concrete and task-relevant (resolve-and-act), in contrast to arbitrary style directives ('reply in French') which it ignored. The system prompt is a real lever for behavioral routing guidance, not cosmetics.

items.question: Besides the run-state bug, the eval flagged a secondary kgsm issue that cripples crash diagnosis. What is it?
choices: run_health_check never reads logs at all
run_health_check skips the log scan when the instance isn't running, yet a crashed server is by definition stopped
run_health_check scans the logs of the wrong instance
run_health_check requires root and silently fails
items.gold: run_health_check skips the log scan when the instance isn't running. But a crashed server is, by definition, stopped — so the number-one troubleshooting case (diagnose a crash from its logs) can never scan logs.

items.question: The RAG design exposes a single `search` tool rather than separate web_search and local-docs tools. What is the stated reason?
choices: It saves VRAM by loading one fewer model
Two overlapping 'search-for-info' tools are exactly the small-model tool-selection failure mode
Web search was removed from the product entirely
It avoids constructing a second HTTP client
items.gold: Overlapping tools are the small-model selection failure. Two 'search-for-info' tools is that failure. One tool = one 'look it up' decision; the backend decides local-vs-web deterministically.

items.question: Which embedding model is the RAG default, and what is the rationale?
choices: nomic-embed-text, chosen for raw speed
bge-m3, chosen for multilingual coverage
embeddinggemma, Gemma-native to cohere with the gemma4 chat model
An OpenAI hosted embedding model
items.gold: embeddinggemma default embedder (Google's Gemma-native on-device model; 768-dim, Matryoshka-truncatable) to pair with gemma4. Built for on-device RAG; coheres with the chat model.

items.question: What couples the standalone indexer to the assistant's retrieval, and what happens when their versions or embedding models disagree?
choices: A shared in-memory cache that is migrated in place
A versioned on-disk index header; on any mismatch the reader rejects it and rebuilds, never migrating
A REST call that retries on mismatch
A database whose schema auto-upgrades
items.gold: The decoupling contract is a versioned on-disk index — header carries format-version + embedding-model + dim + manifest; the reader rejects on any mismatch. Two binaries built at different times must fail loud, not mis-read.

items.question: If local retrieval finds nothing above threshold and the web fallback also returns nothing, what must the `search` tool do?
choices: Return the closest low-relevance chunk dressed up as the answer
Return an explicit 'no relevant sources found' and never fabricate
Silently return an empty string
Keep retrying with relaxed thresholds until something matches
items.gold: If nothing clears MinScore and web fallback also returns nothing, search returns an explicit 'no relevant sources found' — never a fabricated or low-relevance chunk dressed as an answer. The model says it couldn't find that in the docs; it doesn't guess.

items.question: Why is retrieval implemented as a tool the model elects to call, instead of always-on injection before every turn?
choices: Always-on injection is too slow for the RTX 3060
The assistant's traffic is mostly operational, not knowledge Q&A, so retrieval is gated per turn
The model cannot handle injected context windows
It avoids paying for embeddings on idle turns
items.gold: The assistant's traffic is mostly operational (get_status, server_command), not knowledge Q&A. The benchmark's always-retrieve model assumes every query is a doc question; ours aren't. Retrieval must be gated per turn.
